subject: Marketplace procurement roadmap — AWS/Azure/GCP offers & billing path
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Blueway Analytics Procurement <procurement@blueway.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace procurement roadmap — AWS/Azure/GCP offers & billing path

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Blueway's evaluation usage pattern (short bursts, heavy embedding volume for analytics) maps well to our dedicated + marketplace offers. To keep procurement moving, I sketched a pragmatic MAP that covers marketplace private offers (AWS/Azure/GCP), billing options, and the key procurement steps your finance/legal team will need.

High-level ask: can you confirm whether your procurement prefers a consolidated vendor invoice (Redwood billing) or a marketplace-managed invoice (AWS/Azure/GCP charge through their billing)? That decision determines whether we proceed with a Private Offer (marketplace PO) or a standard vendor PO + contract.

Proposed evaluation & close timeline (suggested):
- Week 0 (this week): Procurement form from Blueway + scope confirmation
- Week 1: Redwood sends marketplace pricing private-offer draft (if marketplace billing chosen) or standard contract + PO template
- Week 2: Legal review / SOC2 evidence exchange / SSO & entitlements scoping
- Week 3: DocuSign + finance issues PO / marketplace accept; provisioning and scheduled ramp-up

I've attached a concise checklist (Redwood_Private_Offer_Checklist.pdf) indicating the docs each path requires. Ben, adding you here for quick note on required vm/GPU sizing if Blueway goes with dedicated capacity.

Next step: Asha — if you can return your procurement form and indicate billing preference by end of day Friday, we'll prepare the appropriate offer.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--Attachment: Redwood_Private_Offer_Checklist.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: Blueway Analytics Procurement <procurement@blueway.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Mehra <asha.mehra@blueway.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement roadmap — AWS/Azure/GCP offers & billing path

Hi Diego / Marissa / Ben,

Thanks — attached is our standard procurement intake form. Blueway prefers marketplace-managed billing where possible because it simplifies internal chargeback to product teams, but we are open to direct vendor invoices if the marketplace path materially increases risk/cost.

Attached: Blueway_Procurement_Form.pdf

Asha Mehra
Head of Procurement, Blueway Analytics
asha.mehra@blueway.com
--Attachment: Blueway_Procurement_Form.pdf (pdf, 210KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehra <asha.mehra@blueway.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement roadmap — Marketplace path looks best for Blueway

Asha — appreciate the form and the note on marketplace billing. Given Blueway's preference, here are two parallel tracks so we don't block on legal questions:

1) Marketplace Private Offer path (preferred):
   - Redwood prepares Private Offer pricing for AWS Marketplace (also possible for Azure/GCP).
   - Blueway accepts the private offer in the marketplace; charges flow through AWS/Azure/GCP to your finance.
   - Redwood provides SOC2 + audit artifacts and an MSA addendum to align on data handling.
   - Timeline: Private offer draft in 3 business days once internal pricing approvals are confirmed.

2) Vendor invoice path (fallback):
   - Standard Redwood contract + PO. Redwood bills Blueway directly and issues consolidated monthly invoice.
   - Requires PO + AP contact; typically 7–10 business days more for invoicing cadence setup.

MAP (mutual action plan) — key milestones we propose:
- Day 0: Procurement form received (done)
- Day 2–3: Redwood sends marketplace private-offer draft + DocuSign link for the MSA addendum
- Day 6–9: Blueway legal signs / marketplace accept; finance confirms billing route; marketplace account linkage validated
- Day 10–14: Provisioning + start of evaluation period (10–14 days POC)

Ben — can you confirm the minimum reserved capacity we should include in the PO for predictable latency during the evaluation? Karthik — if any marketplace-specific items (SKU limits, listing requirements) should be called out, please add.

Diego
--Related link: https://hubspot.com/deals/12345-BW
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Asha Mehra <asha.mehra@blueway.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace procurement roadmap — technical sizing note

Quick technical note to include in the MAP:

- For Blueway's evaluation (embedding-heavy, median seq len 96): recommend a baseline reserved capacity equivalent to 4 vGPU workers (NVIDIA A10s or similar) for predictable p50 latency under load.
- If you take the marketplace private offer we can include a short-term burst allowance (2–3x) controlled by policy to handle peak batch jobs during evaluation.
- Required items for provisioning: marketplace account ARN (AWS) or subscription ID (Azure/GCP), SSO service account email for entitlements, and target region(s) for hosting.

I'll attach a short PO template for finance to speed up the vendor-invoice fallback path.

Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
--Attachment: PO_Template.docx (docx, 45KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Blueway Analytics Procurement <procurement@blueway.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement roadmap — legal & billing checklist

Hi Asha / team,

From legal/finance perspective, here are the minimum items we will need, depending on path chosen: 

Marketplace Private Offer path:
- Marketplace acceptance in your account (we will send a private-offer link).
- Signed MSA addendum (DocuSign) covering data residency and support SLAs.
- SOC 2 (Type II) report and data processing addendum (we'll provide links).
- For finance: billing alias / chargeback code so AWS/Azure/GCP can route costs to the right internal BU.

Vendor invoice path:
- Signed MSA + PO referencing Redwood invoice terms (net 30 default; can negotiate net 45).
- AP contact and remittance details.

Notes: marketplace billing is faster for procurement acceptance, but some enterprise accounting teams prefer vendor invoices for audit trails. If Blueway uses the AWS marketplace, we can set the invoice to be consolidated under your consolidated billing if you prefer.

I'll prepare a brief DocuSign envelope for the MSA addendum and a checklist for AP to expedite the PO if you choose the vendor route.

Marissa Cole
Director, Business Operations | Redwood Inference
--Related link: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/BW-PO-2026
--Attachment: Redwood_Private_Offer_Checklist.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Mehra <asha.mehra@blueway.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement roadmap — confirming timeline & next steps

Asha — thanks for the quick coordination. Per your procurement note yesterday, Blueway will accept marketplace-managed billing on AWS. Our plan to hit your target timeline (start evaluation by 9/13) is below: 

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Redwood: send AWS private-offer link + DocuSign MSA addendum (target: 9/9)
- Blueway: marketplace admin accepts private offer + provide marketplace account ARN (target: 9/10)
- Blueway finance: confirm chargeback code and AP contact (target: 9/10)

Evaluation window: 9/13–9/27 (14 days POC). KPIs to validate during POC: embedding throughput per dollar, p50/p95 latency under 2k qps synthetic load, and model accuracy vs baseline prompts (we will run the evaluation harness).

I'll follow up with the private-offer link and DocuSign envelope shortly. If anything changes on your side with the week-1 acceptance timeline, ping me and we'll switch to the vendor-invoice fallback.

Best,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
